requestedActions.title: List active task titles for the connected Todoist account, following pagination

guide.summary: Use Todoist OAuth with only the data:read scope to list active tasks from each connecting customer's own account, then follow cursor pagination on GET /api/v1/tasks. Test with one representative Todoist account before any customer rollout. Provider review, customer workspace approval and listing requirements are not established by the supplied sources and remain unknowns.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List active task titles for the connected Todoist account, following pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Todoist OAuth authorization URL is documented
findings.detail: The authorization request is sent to the Todoist authorize endpoint with client_id, scope, state and response_type=code. Users are redirected to that URL.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint

findings.title: Request data:read for task listing
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks. Request only this scope for the listing use case.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
Get Tasks Get all active tasks for the user.

findings.title: Do not request broader write scopes
findings.detail: data:read_write, data:delete and task:add are broader grants. The listing use case does not need them, and the prohibitions exclude writes.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.

findings.title: Active task listing endpoint is documented
findings.detail: GET /api/v1/tasks returns all active tasks for the user and is paginated with a cursor. Use the same parameters on every page.

evidence.quote: Get Tasks Get all active tasks for the user.
get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks
Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.

steps.title: Register the Todoist app for OAuth
steps.detail: Create the app in Todoist app management and set the redirect URI and scope data:read. Save the client ID and client secret.
steps.doneWhen: The app shows a client ID, a registered redirect URI and data:read as the requested scope.

evidence.quote: "redirect_uris": ["https://example.com/callback"], "scope": "data:read_write",
"grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"], "response_types": ["code"],

steps.title: Implement the authorization redirect and callback
steps.detail: Build the authorize URL with scope=data:read, a random state value and response_type=code. Store the code from the callback, and prepare the token exchange without executing it yet.
steps.doneWhen: The callback receives an authorization code and rejects a mismatched state value.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint

steps.title: Authorize a representative test Todoist account
steps.detail: Use one developer-owned test account to approve the app. Confirm the consent screen requests only data:read.
steps.doneWhen: The callback receives a code for the test account and the granted scope is data:read.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code

steps.title: List the first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Exchange the code for an access token, then request the first page of active tasks. Expected response: a results array and a next_cursor field. Boundary check: confirm the granted scope is data:read only, and confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/tasks.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns active task objects with ids and content, and the request log shows only GET calls.

evidence.quote: curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
Get Tasks Get all active tasks for the user.
get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks

fields: YOUR_TOKEN: OAuth access token from the test authorization

steps.title: Follow the cursor to the next page of tasks
steps.detail: Repeat the request with the same limit and filters plus the next_cursor value. Keep requesting until the response has no next_cursor value. Expected response: the next page of results. Boundary check: confirm the same token is used and no non-GET request is sent.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are followed until next_cursor is absent or null, and the collected titles match the number of tasks across pages.

evidence.quote: Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?cursor=eyJwYWdlIjoyLCJsaW1pdCI6NTB9.aGFzaA&limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.
response as the cursor value for the next request.

fields: NEXT_CURSOR: next_cursor value from the previous response
